messages:
emily: Quick RFC follow-up — proposing we add project-scoped API keys but keep a backward-compatible shim. Two concrete approaches: (A) full namespace: separate key namespace per project (new API surface), or (B) claim-based: add a `proj_id` claim to tokens minted from org keys and enforce at authorizer. Which wins on migration complexity and least surprise?

raj: I lean towards (A) for clarity — a key that literally belongs to proj X is simple to reason about. Downside is migration and more surface area for support. How do we guarantee cross-project service calls without adding wildcard chaos?

sam: +1 for (B) claim-based. Minimal SDK changes (add claim when minting), authorizer checks `proj_id` and sets request context. Migration is easier — existing org keys still work, new tokens can be short-lived scoped tokens. We can add an opt-in header for stricter enforcement.

claire: Main worry with (B) is auditability and rotation. If org keys can mint scoped tokens, audit logs must capture "who minted" and which principal requested it. Also need TTL defaults and a clear rotation story for long-lived vendor tokens.

ops-bot: FYI: any change that adds token variants will affect rate-limiting buckets, quota reporting, and cost attribution. Please file an ops checklist.

raj: For Dedicated/private customers we can't always run a public minting service. We should support a local translation shim (token-translation service) that runs in customer VPC: accepts org key, issues scoped token locally with signed metadata. That preserves isolation.

emily: Sketching a middle-ground: adopt (B) as the logical model (claims + authorizer) and provide two implementations: a hosted minting service and a local translation shim for Private/Dedicated. Token shape: `scope` array with items like `org:ORG_ID`, `proj:PROJ_ID`, `svc:SVC_ID`. Endpoints accept either a legacy org key or a scoped token; enforcement layer checks `scope` and `X-Auth-Mode` header if present (canary).

sam: For RBAC mapping: we should translate `proj:ID` -> role bindings. Example mapping rule (pseudo):
```
if token.scope contains "proj:123" then grant roles: ["project-reader"]
if token.scope contains "svc:billing" then grant roles: ["project-admin"]
```
Also enforce least-privilege: tokens should not inherit org-wide admin unless explicitly minted.

claire: Edge cases: cross-project batch jobs (e.g., nightly ETL) will need explicit service bindings rather than implicit cross-proj access. Suggest a pre-approved binding where admin in both projects can create a `service-binding` that allows a token to include multiple `proj:` entries and an audit trail is created.

raj: Migration proposal: 1) implement claim-based authorizer, 2) release hosted minting + translation shim, 3) add telemetry (how many calls use legacy keys), 4) 6-month opt-in deprecation window for unscoped enforcement. Ops + support playbook required.

emily: OK. Next steps: I'll open an RFC addendum with the recommended approach (claim-based primary + translation shim for private), an outline of token shape, and a migration timeline. Also file SDK task to add mint/refresh helpers. Thanks — will share links when I have the draft. :thumbsup:

ops-bot: Checklist ticket created: https://redwood.internal/ops/ISSUE-4123 (rate limit mapping + billing tags)

sam: small nit — ensure we support both `kid` for key lookup and `iss` to distinguish minted vs legacy keys in logs.

emily: good call. include `minted_by` in audit event model. I'll add that.
